name: Active Dictionary
summary: A reading and vocabulary tool for adult language learners: open a text, PDF or captioned YouTube video, get explanations in context, save expressions with the sentence they came from, then use them in AI conversation and writing practice about the same material.

value: reading work or study material in another language
building vocabulary from your own texts, PDFs and videos
speaking and writing practice about material you've read
Works with texts, PDFs and YouTube videos that have captions
Look up words and ask about difficult passages beside the open material
Personal dictionary that keeps each saved expression with its context
AI chat for follow-up questions about a text
Speaking practice: discuss the material with an AI character, with your saved phrases to hand
Writing tasks with hints on grammar, spelling, punctuation, word choice and style
Public library usable without an account; browser extension and mobile app for saving and reviewing words

value.notes: The privacy policy (effective 1 March 2025) doesn't mention AI, model providers or training; it lists user content among data collected and "improve features and performance" among uses.

answers.note: Privacy policy doesn't address AI training.

answers.note: Built for individual adult learners; no staff, teacher or institution accounts are described.

answers.note: Built for individual adult learners; no staff, teacher or institution accounts are described.

answers.note: Built for individual adult learners; no staff, teacher or institution accounts are described.

answers.question: How it responds to learners
answers.value: In writing practice the learner writes the response; the tool gives hints and the learner decides which changes to make.

answers.question: Answers from your own course content
answers.value: Yes: explanations, chat and speaking practice work from the text, PDF or video the learner has open.

answers.question: Who owns what the AI produces
answers.note: Terms say users keep ownership of content they submit, create or store, with a licence to the company to run and improve the service; AI-generated output isn't addressed.

accessibility.finding: No accessibility standard or conformance report is named on the pages we opened.

security.finding: No security certifications are named on the pages we opened.

dataResidency.finding: The operator is based in Hong Kong, and the privacy policy says information may be processed in other countries with appropriate safeguards. No hosting provider or storage location is named. The policy states it adheres to the GDPR.

ai.finding: The site describes an AI chat, an AI conversation partner and writing hints, but names no AI provider or model, and the privacy policy doesn't say whether learner content or chats train AI models.

procurementChecks: Ask which AI providers process learner text, chats and voice, and whether any of it trains models.
Ask how long chats, recordings and uploaded material are kept.
Confirm the minimum age for learners.

researchTasks: Submitted at /submit on 13 Nov 2026 by Dmitry Yurkin, CTO, Active Dictionary Company Limited, for AI for Learning. Individual adult learners (18+, B1 and above); not an LMS or authoring tool; no institutional deployment claimed. Demo only: public access, no reviewer account, so profile only, not an evaluation.

Submission says there's ongoing free access with paid features, no card needed to start, and AI usage limits; no pricing page found and the terms say only that some features may be paid. Ask for a page to cite.
Submission mentions spaced repetition for saved words; not described on the public pages (the mobile app is for reviewing saved words). Ask where it's documented.
Which languages can people learn? The site shows English–Russian and Russian–English dictionaries and an English interface only.

Age: submission says 18+, privacy policy (effective 1 March 2025) says 13+ (16+ where required). Shown as research ongoing, not a conflict, while the vendor confirms and updates the policy (emailed 13 Nov 2026).
Ask: AI providers and models, training on learner content, retention of chats and voice, and who owns AI-generated output.
Vendor states it supplies no independent evidence of learning outcomes.
